_meta._note: Description backfill for benchmarks with >=8 scores and no description; name/category/metric copied from the DB unchanged. File name sorts last so these declarations win.

benchmarks.name: Arena Vision Elo
benchmarks.description: LMArena (arena.ai) Vision Arena Elo: crowdsourced, blind pairwise human-preference rating of vision-language models on user-submitted prompts that include images; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: EQ-Bench Creative Writing Longform
benchmarks.description: EQ-Bench Longform Creative Writing: an LLM-judged benchmark in which the model plans a short story/novella from a minimal prompt, reflects and revises the plan, then writes it over 8 turns of ~1000 words; the final score (higher is better) is judged by Claude Sonnet 4.6 (v1.11) with penalties such as degradation.

benchmarks.name: LegalBench (Vals-run)
benchmarks.description: Vals AI's independent run of LegalBench, the collaboratively built legal-reasoning benchmark of 162 tasks covering six types of legal reasoning; reported as accuracy (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Vals.ai SWE-Bench Verified
benchmarks.description: Vals AI's independent run of SWE-bench Verified (500 human-validated real GitHub issues), where models given only a bash tool must produce a patch that passes the repository's unit tests; reported as % resolved, higher is better (archived by Vals as saturated).

benchmarks.name: Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2
benchmarks.description: Vals AI Finance Agent v2: an agentic benchmark of 927 expert-reviewed questions testing whether a model can do the work of an entry-level financial analyst by answering difficult questions on public company filings; accuracy (%), higher is better (superseded by v2.1).

benchmarks.name: Aider Polyglot (6-language code gen)
benchmarks.description: Aider Polyglot: 225 challenging Exercism coding exercises across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust, testing whether an LLM can write and edit code correctly via aider without human intervention; percent of exercises solved, higher is better.

benchmarks.name: CyberGym (vuln-reproduction success rate)
benchmarks.description: CyberGym: a large-scale cybersecurity benchmark of 1,507 real-world vulnerabilities across 188 software projects in which an agent, given a vulnerability description and the codebase, must generate a proof-of-concept that reproduces the vulnerability; success rate (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Online-Mind2Web (live web agents)
benchmarks.description: Online-Mind2Web: an online web-agent benchmark of 300 diverse, realistic tasks on 136 live websites, scored by task success rate (human or LLM-as-a-judge evaluation); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Fiction.liveBench
benchmarks.description: Fiction.liveBench: a long-context comprehension benchmark built from stories on Fiction.live, where each question requires theory of mind for characters, tracking chronology and inference from implicit information; accuracy (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: ScreenSpot-Pro (high-res GUI grounding)
benchmarks.description: ScreenSpot-Pro: a GUI-grounding benchmark of expert-annotated high-resolution screenshots from 23 professional applications across five industries and three operating systems, where the model must locate the target UI element; accuracy (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Arena Search Elo
benchmarks.description: LMArena (arena.ai) Search Arena Elo: crowdsourced, in-the-wild pairwise human-preference rating of search-augmented LLM systems, with prompts focused on current events and real-world use; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: VPCT
benchmarks.description: VPCT (Visual Physics Comprehension Test): 100 simulator-generated images each showing a ball, ramps and three buckets; the model must predict which bucket the ball falls into; accuracy (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Gray Swan IPI (indirect prompt injection ASR)
benchmarks.description: Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark: about 1,800 highly transferable attacks across 37 scenarios (coding, tool use, GUI computer use) that try to induce harmful actions such as data exfiltration; reported as attack success rate, mostly at k=15 attempts; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: HBM Memory Bandwidth
benchmarks.description: Hardware specification: peak memory bandwidth of an AI accelerator in TB/s (HBM for datacenter parts; some rows are GDDR or unified memory), taken from vendor/press spec sheets; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: HBM Memory Capacity
benchmarks.description: Hardware specification: on-package high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity of an AI accelerator in GB, taken from vendor/press spec sheets; higher is more memory.

benchmarks.name: file_size_gb_lower_better
benchmarks.description: Not a benchmark: the on-disk file size (GB) of a quantized GGUF build of a model (one row per quant type, e.g. Q4_K_M), as listed in Hugging Face GGUF repositories such as bartowski and Unsloth; lower is smaller.

benchmarks.name: Disordered eating — API single-turn harmless
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: share of single-turn disordered-eating prompts posing potential risk where the model's response was harmless, run on the API without a system prompt, across all tested languages; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Disordered eating — API benign over-refusal
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: refusal rate on benign single-turn questions about nutrition, fitness and health in the disordered-eating domain, run on the API without a system prompt; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Bio Refusal Eval — Dual Use
benchmarks.description: OpenAI system-card Biology Model Refusal Evaluation, Dual Use split: 0-1 safety score for model-only responses (no production safeguards) to dual-use biology prompts drawn from held-out synthetic, red-teaming and production data; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Codeforces Rating (AI)
benchmarks.description: Codeforces rating: a vendor-reported, Elo-style competitive-programming rating from Codeforces problems (e.g. DeepSeek's internal Codeforces benchmark); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Peak FP8 Dense PFLOPS
benchmarks.description: Hardware specification: vendor peak FP8 tensor throughput of an AI accelerator (or rack system) in PFLOPS, intended as dense (non-sparse) figures; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cosmos Hue I2V
benchmarks.description: Cosmos HUE (HUman Evaluation), image-to-video: NVIDIA's human scoring protocol on 100 PAIBench-G prompts (5 seeds each), where annotators answer atomic Yes/No questions on semantic alignment, physical laws, geometric reasoning and visual integrity; % passed, higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Disordered eating — claude.ai single-turn harmless
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: share of single-turn disordered-eating prompts posing potential risk where the model's response was harmless, run on claude.ai with its default system prompt; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Disordered eating — claude.ai benign over-refusal
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: refusal rate on benign single-turn disordered-eating-domain questions (nutrition, fitness, health), run on claude.ai; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Election integrity — benign API overrefusal
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card election-integrity eval: refusal rate on the 300 benign election-related prompts of the single-turn election integrity benchmark, run on the API without a system prompt; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Mmlu Med
benchmarks.description: MMLU Med: the medical subset of MMLU (Anatomy, Clinical Knowledge, College Biology, College Medicine, Medical Genetics, Professional Medicine, Virology) of multiple-choice questions, used in MedGemma evaluations (3,685 examples); accuracy, higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Paibench G T2V Domain
benchmarks.description: PAIBench-G text-to-video Domain Score: VLM-as-judge (Qwen2.5-VL-72B in the Cosmos 3 report) binary checks of physical and semantic accuracy on the 1,044-prompt video-generation track of the Physical AI Benchmark across six domains; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Single-turn benign — claude.ai overrefusal
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card eval: over-refusal rate on single-turn benign but sensitive requests covering 16 policy areas in seven languages, run on claude.ai; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Suicide/self-harm — claude.ai single-turn harmless rate
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: harmless response rate on single-turn suicide/self-harm prompts posing potential risk, run on claude.ai; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Suicide/self-harm — claude.ai multi-turn appropriate
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: appropriate response rate in multi-turn conversations about suicide and self-harm, run on claude.ai; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Suicide/self-harm — claude.ai benign over-refusal
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card safety eval: refusal rate on benign single-turn requests in the suicide/self-harm domain, run on claude.ai; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Atlas TW (Test Writing)
benchmarks.description: Scale AI SWE Atlas - Test Writing: a SEAL leaderboard benchmark of an agent's ability to write production-grade tests for real codebases, part of the SWE Atlas suite; score (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: TTS Arena V2 Elo (HuggingFace TTS-AGI)
benchmarks.description: TTS Arena V2 Elo (Hugging Face TTS-AGI): crowdsourced blind pairwise rating of text-to-speech models, where voters hear two anonymous models read the same text and pick the more human-sounding one; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cosmos Hue T2V
benchmarks.description: Cosmos HUE (HUman Evaluation), text-to-video: NVIDIA's human scoring protocol on 100 PAIBench-G prompts (5 seeds each), where annotators answer atomic Yes/No questions on semantic alignment, physical laws, geometric reasoning and visual integrity; % passed, higher is better.

benchmarks.name: HAL Composite (cost-controlled accuracy)
benchmarks.description: Not a published HAL metric but a composite built in this repo: the mean of a model's best accuracy across the Princeton HAL (Holistic Agent Leaderboard) sub-leaderboards it appears on (e.g. AssistantBench, CORE-Bench Hard, GAIA, Online Mind2Web, SWE-bench Verified Mini, SciCode, ScienceAgentBench, TAU-bench Airline, USACO); higher is better. Coverage varies by model.

benchmarks.name: Japanese Mt Bench
benchmarks.description: Japanese MT-Bench: Stability AI's Japanese version of MT-Bench, 80 challenging open-ended multi-turn questions across writing, roleplay, reasoning, math, coding, extraction, STEM and humanities, graded by a GPT-4-class judge on a 1-10 scale; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Kimi Code Bench v2
benchmarks.description: Kimi Code Bench 2.0 (KCB 2.0): Moonshot AI's internal benchmark of code agents on realistic, end-to-end software engineering tasks across many programming languages and production technology stacks; score (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Paibench G T2V Quality
benchmarks.description: PAIBench-G text-to-video Quality Score: aggregate of frame consistency, motion smoothness, aesthetic quality and video-text alignment on the 1,044-prompt video-generation track of the Physical AI Benchmark; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Rbench I2V
benchmarks.description: RBench image-to-video: a robotics video-generation benchmark of 650 image-text cases (250 task-oriented, 400 embodiment-specific) scoring task completion and visual quality of generated robot-object interaction videos; score (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: USACO Competitive Programming
benchmarks.description: USACO: 307 competitive-programming problems from the USA Computing Olympiad with exhaustive test cases, used on the Princeton HAL leaderboard to evaluate agents; accuracy (% solved), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cosmos Hue I2V Robotics Domain
benchmarks.description: Robotics-domain breakdown of Cosmos HUE image-to-video (Rob. column of the per-domain HUE I2V leaderboard): % of atomic human-verified Yes/No questions passed on robotics prompts; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: MRCR v2 (8-needle)
benchmarks.description: MRCR v2 (8-needle): the 8-needle setting of multi-round co-reference resolution, where the model must return a specific instance among 8 identical asks hidden in a long synthetic multi-turn conversation; scored by match similarity at the stated context length (e.g. 128k average or 1M), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Paibench G T2V
benchmarks.description: PAIBench-G text-to-video overall score (0.5 x Quality + 0.5 x Domain) on the 1,044-prompt video-generation track of the Physical AI Benchmark across six Physical AI domains, extended to T2V in the Cosmos 3 report; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Atlas RF (Refactor)
benchmarks.description: Scale AI SWE Atlas - Refactoring: a benchmark of an agent's ability to restructure production code while preserving behavior, graded by existing tests and rubric criteria (maintainability, documentation, cleanup, no regressions); score (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: BigBench Extra Hard (BBEH)
benchmarks.description: BIG-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH): replaces each BIG-Bench Hard task with a harder novel task probing a similar reasoning skill, to measure broad general reasoning; accuracy (EM), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Frontierswe
benchmarks.description: FrontierSWE: a long-horizon software engineering benchmark of very hard tasks (V2: 34 tasks, 5 trials per task with a 20-hour budget); DB values are mostly vendor-reported (e.g. dominance scores in the Kimi K3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Hpsv3
benchmarks.description: HPSv3 (Human Preference Score v3): a VLM-based human-preference reward model trained on 1.17M pairwise comparisons (HPDv3), used as a prompt-aware text-to-image quality metric; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Peak BF16/FP16 Dense TFLOPS
benchmarks.description: Hardware specification: vendor peak BF16/FP16 tensor throughput of an AI accelerator in TFLOPS, intended as dense (non-sparse) figures; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Ko Longbench
benchmarks.description: Ko-LongBench: LG AI Research's in-house benchmark of Korean long-context understanding, with Document QA, Story Understanding, Dialogue History Understanding, In-Context Learning, Structured QA and RAG tasks; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Paibench G I2V
benchmarks.description: PAIBench-G image-to-video overall score (0.5 x Quality + 0.5 x Domain) on the 1,044 image-text prompt pairs of the Physical AI Benchmark video-generation track across six Physical AI domains; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Robolab Overall Specific
benchmarks.description: RoboLab-120 overall task success rate (%) with specific instructions: a simulation benchmark of 120 language-conditioned manipulation tasks for generalist robot policies (DROID-finetuned policies in the Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Texture CMMD (CLIP-MMD)
benchmarks.description: Texture CMMD (CLIP Maximum-Mean Discrepancy): a texture-generation metric used in the Hunyuan3D 2.0/2.5 papers to assess the diversity and richness of generated texture details against ground truth; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Texture FID-CLIP
benchmarks.description: Texture CLIP-FID: Fréchet distance in CLIP feature space between rendered generated textures and ground truth, used in the Hunyuan3D 2.0/2.5 texture comparisons; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Texture LPIPS
benchmarks.description: Texture LPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity) between rendered generated textures and ground truth, used in the Hunyuan3D 2.0/2.5 texture comparisons; lower is better.

benchmarks.name: anthropic_mask_honesty_resist_pressure
benchmarks.description: Anthropic system-card run of MASK (public test split): honesty rate, i.e. the fraction of scored prompts (~800) where the model did not contradict its own elicited belief under user or system-prompt pressure; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: BigCodeBench
benchmarks.description: BigCodeBench: 1,140 fine-grained Python tasks that require invoking multiple function calls from 139 libraries across 7 domains, checked by test cases; Pass@1 (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cosmos Soundbench Avq
benchmarks.description: Cosmos-SoundBench Audiovisual Quality (AVQ): overall score on 144 non-speech FoleyBench-derived prompts for audio-video generation, defined as 0.5 x SAV (semantic audiovisual score) + 0.5 x audio quality, on a 0-10 scale; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cosmos Soundbench Pq
benchmarks.description: Cosmos-SoundBench Production Quality (PQ): audiobox-aesthetics production-quality score of generated audio (clarity, fidelity, dynamics, bandwidth, spatialization) on the 144-prompt benchmark, 0-10 scale; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cosmos Soundbench Sav
benchmarks.description: Cosmos-SoundBench Semantic Audiovisual score (SAV): MLLM-judged 0.60 x semantic audio correctness + 0.30 x audiovisual alignment + 0.10 x visual support on the 144-prompt benchmark, 0-10 scale; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cvtg 102Ch Gned
benchmarks.description: CVTG-102ch GNED: OCR-based normalized-edit-distance accuracy of rendered scene text on a 102-prompt Chinese-character subset of the Complex Visual Text Generation benchmark (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cvtg 102Ch Pned
benchmarks.description: CVTG-102ch PNED: character-level OCR normalized-edit-distance accuracy on the 102-prompt Chinese-character subset of the Complex Visual Text Generation benchmark (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cvtg 500L Gned
benchmarks.description: CVTG-500L GNED: OCR-based normalized-edit-distance accuracy of rendered scene text on 500 English prompts sampled from CVTG-2K and upsampled into long, dense descriptions (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Cvtg 500L Pned
benchmarks.description: CVTG-500L PNED: character-level OCR normalized-edit-distance accuracy on the 500-prompt English long-prompt CVTG subset (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: ExploitGym (2h budget)
benchmarks.description: ExploitGym (2-hour budget): number of the benchmark's 869 real-world vulnerabilities (userspace, V8, Linux kernel) for which the agent builds a working exploit that captures a secret flag via the intended vulnerability within two hours, mitigations disabled; count, higher is better.

benchmarks.name: MLS Bench Lite
benchmarks.description: MLS-Bench-Lite: a 30-task challenging subset (covering all 12 domains) of MLS-Bench, which tests whether AI agents can invent generalizable and scalable ML methods by improving a targeted component of an ML system; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: OTIS-AIME 2025
benchmarks.description: OTIS Mock AIME: competition math problems from the OTIS (Olympiad Training for Individual Study) Mock AIME exams, each with an integer answer 0-999, harder than MATH Level 5; accuracy (%), higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Robolab Complex Specific
benchmarks.description: RoboLab-120 task success rate (%) on Complex-difficulty tasks with specific instructions, from the 120-task language-conditioned robot manipulation simulation benchmark (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Robolab Overall Default
benchmarks.description: RoboLab-120 overall task success rate (%) with default instructions, from the 120-task language-conditioned robot manipulation simulation benchmark (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Robolab Overall Vague
benchmarks.description: RoboLab-120 overall task success rate (%) with vague instructions, from the 120-task language-conditioned robot manipulation simulation benchmark (Cosmos 3 report); higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Toys4k Text-to-3D CLIP
benchmarks.description: Toys4k text-to-3D CLIP score: consistency between generated 3D assets and their text prompts on the held-out Toys4k dataset, as used in the TRELLIS paper; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Toys4k Text-to-3D FD-DINOv2
benchmarks.description: Toys4k text-to-3D FD-DINOv2: Fréchet distance with DINOv2 features between renders of generated 3D assets and Toys4k references, measuring overall generation quality (TRELLIS paper); lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Unigenbench Orig
benchmarks.description: UniGenBench (original 600 prompts): text-to-image semantic-consistency benchmark spanning 5 themes and 20 subthemes; score is the MLLM-judged (Gemini 3.1 Pro in the Cosmos 3 report) fraction of testpoints passed; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Unigenbench Phys
benchmarks.description: UniGenBench-Phys: 570 NVIDIA-added photorealistic physical-world text-to-image prompts (robotics, signage, driving, construction, fluids, medical) scored as the MLLM-judged fraction of testpoints passed; higher is better.

benchmarks.name: VisualAgentBench (VAB)
benchmarks.description: VisualAgentBench (VAB): a benchmark of large multimodal models as visual agents across embodied, GUI and visual-design environments; overall average success rate (%), higher is better.
